rationale:
Evidence: the best measured design is iteration 5 (score 137.76, base_speed 1.8, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, 0.8 kg, sensors at y 0.06 with x from -0.06 to +0.06, 16 mm footprints, kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.4, last_direction). Iterations 2 and 4 (base 1.6) scored 132.0, so raising base_speed from 1.6 to 1.8 gained about 5.8 points. Iteration 3 (ki 0.6) scored lower (122.2) than ki 0.3, so larger integral gain has already been tested and did not help. Iterations 1 and 3 (base 1.2 to 1.3 and kd/kp changes) scored lower, and no tested design below base 1.6 has been better.

What I accepted from the round-1 critique: (1) The draft's base_speed 1.3 is below the best measured speed, and the critique correctly says a 3 s completion needs about 1.5 m/s average. I raise base_speed to 1.8, which is the best-evidenced value. (2) The draft changed mass, body length, body width and sensor y at once, so its result could not be attributed to any one change, and the critique notes the body_width argument is wrong (the off-track limit is 0.06 m for any width below 0.19 m). I reject the draft geometry and return to the measured iteration-5 geometry. (3) The draft's ki 1.0 is outside the tested range and runs against the data: ki 0.6 already lowered the score relative to ki 0.3. I reject it and keep ki 0.3. (4) The steady max_error near 0.06 with flat rms may be a motor-mismatch bias, but the one-step test for that is a smaller ki, not a larger one; this is deferred to a later iteration.

What I kept: kp 3.0, kd 0.4, last_direction, sensor span and footprint, and all geometry, so this candidate equals the best measured design. The reason is that a revision built on untested geometry and an untested ki has a worse expected score than the best-evidenced design, and the score (completion, progress, line loss, rms) rewards staying on the line.

Expected result: about 138 points, consistent with iteration 5, with oval progress near 0.55 and completion on rare oval runs. Decision rule for the next round: if progress is again flat and max_error stays at 0.06, the next single-variable test is ki 0.1 (not 1.0). If the line is lost on the s-bend or slalom, test a sensor footprint or span change on those tracks. Base_speed 2.0 is the next speed step only if completion_time is the limit rather than off-track ends.
